tagline: Infrastructure operator transforming capital into recurring cash flows
hero_kpi_rationale: This KPI is central as it reflects Ferrovial's transformation into a recurring cash flow company through its infrastructure assets, a scalable and predictable business model, typical of infrastructure champions.

kpis.name: Dividends from Infrastructure Assets
kpis.explanation: Cash received annually from infrastructure assets such as highways and airports.
kpis.description: Ferrovial received 947 million euros in dividends in 2024, including initial payments from I-77 and I-66 in the United States.
kpis.signal: Historic record in 2024, demonstrates portfolio maturity.

kpis.name: Revenue
kpis.explanation: Total sales realized by the company over the year.
kpis.description: Revenue reached 9.1 billion euros in 2024, up 6.7%.

kpis.name: Adjusted EBITDA
kpis.explanation: Gross operating profit, adjusted for non-recurring items.
kpis.description: Adjusted EBITDA surged 38.9% to 1.3 billion euros, excluding currency effects and scope changes.

kpis.name: Net Profit
kpis.explanation: Profit after all charges, taxes and disposals.
kpis.description: Net profit stands at 3.2 billion euros, driven by gains on asset sales.
kpis.signal: Strongly boosted by long-term asset disposal gains.

kpis.name: Net Debt
kpis.explanation: Total financial debt minus available cash.
kpis.description: Net debt is negative at -1.8 billion euros, indicating a cash surplus position.
kpis.signal: Cash exceeding debt: very solid balance sheet.

kpis.name: Liquidity
kpis.explanation: Available cash, including proceeds from asset disposals.
kpis.description: Liquidity reaches 5.3 billion euros, supported by disposals and dividends.

kpis.name: Shareholder Distributions
kpis.description: Shareholder distributions totaled 895 million euros, including 272 million in share buybacks.

kpis.name: Total Assets
kpis.description: Total assets extracted from yfinance over the last four years.
kpis.signal: Total assets of 27.42 billion euros in the latest year

kpis.name: CO2 Emissions Reduction
kpis.explanation: Decrease in direct and energy emissions compared to 2020.
kpis.description: 35.8% reduction in CO2 emissions (scope 1 and 2) compared to 2020, in line with the 1.5°C trajectory.

kpis.name: Water Consumption Reduction
kpis.explanation: Decrease in water consumption compared to 2017.
kpis.description: 26.7% reduction in water consumption compared to 2017.

risks.title: Reliance on major projects and delay risks
risks.score_rationale: Risk explicitly identified at the beginning of Item 3.D as principal ("reliance on a small number of major projects"). Intensive language: "materially impact", "delayed, terminated". Concrete example: NTO at JFK impacted by Russian airspace closure. High weight for project-based business model.

risks.title: Geopolitical conflicts and instability affecting operations
risks.score_rationale: Major risk in Item 3.D.1.1 with multiple concrete examples. Strong language: "adversely affect", "increased risk of disruption". Specific cases: Budimex in Poland (23.3% of 2025 revenues), armed incident Ruta del Cacao Colombia (December 2025). Upward trend with Ukraine/Middle East conflicts.

risks.title: Economic contraction reducing transport/infrastructure demand
risks.score_rationale: Risk identified Item 3.D.1.2 as principal. Direct language: "slowdown or contraction", "reduction in use and related income". Sensitive sectors: toll roads, airports. Clear causal link with revenues. Significant weight for concession-based model.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and critical technology failures
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned Item 3.D ("cyber threats, technology failures"). Language: "exposes us to cyber threats". Emerging AI risks included. Position in summary of risks indicates growing importance. Applicable to critical digital systems (toll collection, airports, project management).

risks.title: Complex and evolving regulatory compliance
risks.score_rationale: Risk Item 3.D: "regulatory compliance risks" including data protection, anti-corruption, anti-bribery. Language: "complex and evolving tax laws". Multi-jurisdiction operations (Spain, Netherlands, Poland, Colombia, Australia, Canada, India) amplify complexity. High weight for international group.

risks.title: Acquisition/divestment risks and integration
risks.score_rationale: Mentioned Item 3.D: "risks associated with past and future acquisitions or divestments". Moderate but present language. Context: group undergoing restructuring (re-domiciliation Spain to Netherlands 2023). Moderate weight but relevant to growth strategy.

risks.title: Dependence on subcontractors and workforce availability
risks.score_rationale: Risk Item 3.D: "availability and reliability of subcontractors and service providers, access to skilled labor". Language: "face risks from". Relevant for Construction (Budimex) and complex projects. Material inflation mentioned (Ukraine conflicts). High weight for operating model.

risks.title: Intense competition and scarcity of high-value opportunities
risks.score_rationale: Risk Item 3.D: "highly competitive global market where high value opportunities are scarce and competition is intense". Direct but standard language. Moderate weight: applicable to all segments (Construction, Concessions, Services). Stable trend in mature sector.

ai_positioning.summary: Ferrovial makes no mention of any strategy or initiative related to artificial intelligence in its 2024 financial documents.
evidence: No mention of AI in the CEO letter
No reference to AI technologies in infrastructure projects
No KPI or initiative related to automation or predictive analytics
